title: Cayley–Hamilton for a free module of finite rank
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $T$ an indeterminate with polynomial ring $R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $L$ a free $R$-module of finite rank $r$ and $\varphi:L\to L$ an $R$-linear endomorphism. Let $M\in M_r(R)$ be the matrix of $\varphi$ in a basis of $L$ and $\chi_\varphi(T)=\det(T\,I_r-M)\in R[T]$ (independent of the basis). Then $\chi_\varphi$ is monic of degree $r$, and writing $\chi_\varphi=\sum_{i=0}^rc_iT^i$ one has $\sum_{i=0}^rc_i\varphi^i=0$ as an endomorphism of $L$ (Cayley–Hamilton). For $R=\mathbf Z$, $\chi_\varphi\in\mathbf Z[T]$ is a monic polynomial with integer coefficients.
